description: Key facts a correct lesson on each Basic Electronics Engineering topic must state. Every fact was taken from the fetched text of the source page named with it (the quote is checked by `npm run golden:check`). Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions matched against the lesson text after LaTeX backslashes and braces are removed.
subject: basic-electronics

facts.claim: A diode conducts mainly in one direction (forward), blocking reverse

source.quote: conducts electric current primarily in one direction

facts.claim: Significant current only above the forward (cut-in) voltage

source.quote: having a forward threshold voltage or turn-on voltage or cut-in voltage

facts.claim: In reverse, current rises suddenly at the breakdown voltage

source.quote: when the reverse voltage across the diode reaches a value called the breakdown voltage

facts.claim: A Zener diode is used in reverse breakdown

source.quote: A conventional solid-state diode allows significant current if it is reverse biased above its reverse-breakdown voltage

facts.claim: Used as a voltage reference / regulator

source.quote: Zener diodes are widely used as voltage references and as shunt regulators to regulate the voltage across small circuits

facts.claim: Zener effect at low voltage, avalanche breakdown at higher voltage

source.quote: with the Zener effect predominating at lower voltages and avalanche breakdown at higher voltages

facts.claim: A rectifier converts AC to DC

source.quote: converts alternating current (AC), which periodically reverses direction, to direct current (DC)

facts.claim: Half-wave passes one half of the AC wave and blocks the other

source.quote: either the positive or negative half of the AC wave is passed, while the other half is blocked

facts.claim: Three regions: emitter, base and collector

source.quote: The regions of a BJT are called emitter, base, and collector

facts.claim: The emitter is the most heavily doped region

source.quote: the emitter region is heavily doped compared to the other two layers

facts.claim: CE output is 180° out of phase with the input

source.quote: the output signal is 180 degrees out of phase with respect to the input

facts.claim: Base is the input, collector the output, emitter common to both

source.quote: the base terminal of the transistor serves as the input, the collector is the output, and the emitter is common to both

facts.claim: The gate is insulated and its voltage controls conduction

source.quote: It has an insulated gate, the voltage of which determines the conductivity of the device

facts.claim: Gate voltage creates a channel between source and drain

source.quote: The inversion layer provides a channel through which current can pass between source and drain terminals

facts.claim: CMOS uses complementary pairs of p-type and n-type MOSFETs

source.quote: uses complementary and symmetrical pairs of p-type and n-type MOSFETs for logic functions

facts.claim: Very low static power consumption and high noise immunity

source.quote: Two important characteristics of CMOS devices are high noise immunity and low static power consumption

facts.claim: A differential input and extremely high (open-loop) gain

source.quote: a DC-coupled electronic amplifier with a differential input, a (usually) single-ended output voltage, and an extremely high gain

facts.claim: High input impedance and low output impedance

source.quote: high input impedance at the input terminals and low output impedance at the output terminal(s)

facts.claim: With negative feedback, external components set the gain

source.quote: By using negative feedback, the characteristics of an op amp application circuit

facts.claim: NAND is a universal gate: any gate can be made from NANDs

source.quote: A NAND gate is a universal gate, meaning that any other gate can be represented as a combination of NAND gates

facts.claim: NOT(x) = NAND(x, x)

source.quote: the function NOT(x) may be equivalently expressed as NAND(x,x)

facts.claim: NOT(A AND B) = NOT A OR NOT B
facts.pattern: overline\s*A\s*(cdot|·)?\s*B\s*=\s*overline\s*A\s*\+\s*overline\s*B|\(A\s*(·|cdot|\.)?\s*B\)'\s*=\s*A'\s*\+\s*B'|NOT \(?A AND B\)?|not A or not B

source.quote: The negation of "A and B" is the same as "not A or not B"

facts.claim: NOT(A OR B) = NOT A AND NOT B
facts.pattern: overline\s*A\s*\+\s*B\s*=\s*overline\s*A\s*(cdot|·)?\s*overline\s*B|\(A\s*\+\s*B\)'\s*=\s*A'\s*(·|cdot|\.)?\s*B'|NOT \(?A OR B\)?|not A and not B

source.quote: The negation of "A or B" is the same as "not A and not B"

facts.claim: A half adder adds two bits (sum and carry)

source.quote: The half adder adds two single binary digits

facts.claim: A full adder also takes a carry-in; two half adders + OR make one

source.quote: two half adders can be combined to make a full adder

facts.claim: Binary is base 2, using only 0 and 1
facts.pattern: base[- ]?2|radix 2|only (the digits |two digits |two symbols )?0 and 1|digits 0 and 1

source.quote: a method for representing numbers that uses only two symbols for the natural numbers: typically 0 (zero) and 1 (one)

facts.claim: Each binary digit is a bit

source.quote: Each digit is referred to as a bit, or binary digit

facts.claim: In an LED electrons recombine with holes and release photons

source.quote: Electrons in the semiconductor recombine with electron holes, thereby releasing energy in the form of photons

facts.claim: The band gap sets the colour (photon energy)

source.quote: The wavelength of the light depends on the energy band gap of the semiconductors used
